analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation, metadata, patches and added diagnostic source against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. No concrete regression is established in this scope. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md:1147–1155 and fixtures/prompt-contract/glm53-flash/README.md:45–48 describe newly supported GLM controls and post-generation validation rather than constrained decoding; fixtures explicitly do not qualify those modes. Integration must verify fail-closed schema/tool validation and buffering before content or tool exposure, separate reasoning-channel behavior, loaded-model selection and media refusals in the cited implementation (TB-007, T-007, T-056). The documented withheld-output deadline signal also needs checking against actual admission/cancellation behavior (T-010); documentation alone proves neither enforcement nor a bypass.
GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift:35–87 generates fixed sysctl advice and an optional root LaunchDaemon using /usr/sbin/sysctl, not provider-controlled executable paths. Lines 123–145 read limits and restrict recommendations to M5/256-GiB machines; no sysctl mutation, installation, authorization grant or request data logging occurs in this source. Operator-applied advice raises system-wide wired-memory limits persistently; integration should check its callers remain advisory and preserve admission/resource safeguards. This is distinct from the fan-helper authority in TB-010.
Unchanged surrounding protocol text retains encrypted-only request bodies, cache nonce/scope checks, consent-bound autopilot ownership and diagnostic-only trust labels; it supplies no evidence of changed encryption, billing or authorization controls. libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 changes the native-runtime dependency revision, but its internal diff is absent. Review that revision for inference isolation, cache scoping/authentication, cancellation and streaming enforcement (TB-007, T-028, T-041, T-010). This missing dependency source is a material coverage limit, not proof of safety or a vulnerability.
